what: Headings and menu text appear as if typed through an input method — each keystroke takes 29ms (an option) and the composition state grows (for Korean, even the way the final consonant carries over, like ㅇ → 여 → 역 → 여기), and once a word is fully typed, it is ”converted” to the final text after 20ms, the letters sharpening from .58 opacity and 1.2px blur over .075s with power2.out, then it rests 25ms before moving to the next word. For a word written as ”final|reading”, the reading is typed one character at a time and then switches to the final text (kanji or English). Multiple lines run in order (serial), staggered (stagger) or all at once (parallel). While typing, the final text is laid underneath invisibly so the line width does not shift

options.char: Gap per keystroke (ms), default 29. Original header menu 29 · brand 27 · concept title 25 · vertical text 11 · speaker title 32 · timetable 30
options.convert: Delay from word end to transform (ms), default 20 — vertical text 14 · concept title/apply 18
options.mode: With multiple lines: serial (next after the previous finishes) · stagger (default) · parallel
options.stagger: stagger interval (ms), default 55 — vertical text 52 · timetable 95
options.delay: Start delay (ms), default 0 — header menu 140 · brand 360 · vertical text 180
options.on: view (default, once when it enters the screen) · load (immediately) · manual (waits for fx:play)
options.data-fx-part=\"line\": Child row — if none, the element itself is a single row
options.data-text: Line attribute — when giving the reading separately as ”final|reading” (if absent, the line text as is, and Korean is automatically read by jamo composition)
options.fx:play: Sending to the element retypes it from the start · emits fx:typed when done

use: Your title here Second line
note: The original converts typed kana readings into kanji. With Korean placeholder, it uses the jamo composition state as the reading and shows a conversion blur at the end of words of two or more syllables
